questions.question: What is the name of the service unveiled by Reliance Jio Infocomm Limited, India's first satellite-based gigabit broadband service, in October 2023?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jio Space Fiber**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Reliance Jio Infocomm Limited launched India's first satellite-based gigabit broadband service named **Jio Space Fiber** in October 2023.
 
• The service aims to provide high-speed internet connectivity to remote and rural areas across India.
 
• Jio Space Fiber utilizes satellite technology to deliver gigabit speeds, making it possible for users in underserved regions to access reliable broadband services.
 
• This initiative is part of Reliance Jio's broader strategy to enhance digital infrastructure and bridge the digital divide in India.
 
• Jio Space Fiber is expected to play a crucial role in supporting various digital initiatives, including education, healthcare, and e-governance, in remote areas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Satellite Broadband Technology**

 
 
• Satellite broadband uses satellites to provide internet services, especially in remote or rural areas where traditional broadband infrastructure is not available.
 
• It involves the transmission of data signals from a ground station to a satellite, which then relays the signals back to a satellite dish installed at the user's location.
 
• This technology is crucial for ensuring connectivity in areas where laying cables is challenging or economically unfeasible.
 
 
 
• **Digital Divide in India**
 
 
• The digital divide refers to the gap between those who have access to modern information and communication technology and those who do not.
 
• Bridging this divide is essential for ensuring equal opportunities in education, employment, and access to government services.
 
• Initiatives like Jio Space Fiber are instrumental in addressing the digital divide by providing high-speed internet access to underserved regions.
 
 
 
• **Reliance Jio's Digital Initiatives**
 
 
• Reliance Jio has been at the forefront of revolutionizing digital services in India, with a focus on affordable and high-speed internet connectivity.
 
• Jio's various digital initiatives include Jio Fiber, JioPhone, and now Jio Space Fiber, aimed at enhancing internet access and digital infrastructure.
 
• These initiatives have significantly contributed to increasing internet penetration and digital literacy in India.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Remote and Rural Areas**
 
 
• High-speed internet access in remote and rural areas can transform education by enabling online learning and access to global educational resources.
 
• It can improve healthcare services through telemedicine and remote consultation facilities.
 
• Enhanced connectivity also supports local businesses by providing access to broader markets and digital tools for growth.

questions.question: What is term used to refer the ‘exports to foreigners’ in the circular flow of income diagram?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**injection**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In the circular flow of income, exports are considered an **injection** into the economy because they bring in foreign capital.
 
• Injections are factors that contribute positively to the economy's income flow, in contrast to leakages, which reduce it.
 
• By selling goods and services to foreigners, the domestic economy receives payments, which increase the overall income level.
 
• Other examples of injections include government spending and investments by businesses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Leakages**: These are elements that take money out of the circular flow of income, such as savings, taxes, and imports.
 
• **Investment**: This refers to the purchase of goods that are not consumed today but are used in the future to create wealth, such as machinery or buildings.
 
• **Government Spending**: Expenditures by the government on goods and services, which act as injections into the economy.
 
• **Expenditure Approach**: A method for calculating GDP by adding up all the expenditures made in an economy, including consumption, investment, government spending, and net exports.
 
• **Net Exports**: This is the value of a country's total exports minus its total imports, and it is a crucial component of a nation's GDP.

questions.question: After Indian Hockey Federation was dismissed in 2008 by IOA, _________ was formed.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hockey India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Hockey India was formed in 2009, following the dismissal of the Indian Hockey Federation by the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) in 2008.
 
• Hockey India is the governing body for field hockey in India, responsible for the administration of both men’s and women’s hockey.
 
• It is recognized by the International Hockey Federation (FIH) as the national association for field hockey in India.
 
• Hockey India organizes national championships and oversees the development of the sport across the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian Hockey Federation (IHF):**

 
 
• Formed in 1925, the IHF was the original governing body for field hockey in India before its dismissal in 2008.
 
• The IHF was responsible for the administration and promotion of field hockey in India during its tenure.
 
 
 
• **Indian Olympic Association (IOA):**
 
 
• The IOA is the body responsible for selecting athletes to represent India at the Olympic Games, Asian Games, and other international athletic meets.
 
• It played a key role in the formation of Hockey India after the dismissal of the IHF.
 
 
 
• **International Hockey Federation (FIH):**
 
 
• The FIH is the international governing body for field hockey and indoor field hockey.
 
• It works to promote the sport globally and organizes major international tournaments like the Hockey World Cup.
 
 
 
• **National Championships:**
 
 
• These are domestic field hockey tournaments organized by Hockey India to promote the sport at various levels.
 
• They include competitions like the Hockey India League (HIL) and various age-group championships.

questions.question: India’s latitudinal extent is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**8º4' North to 37º6' North latitudes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India's latitudinal extent ranges from **8º4' North to 37º6' North latitudes**.
 
• This range covers approximately **29 degrees of latitude**.
 
• The latitudinal extent influences India's **climate** and **day length** variations.
 
• It plays a significant role in the **diversity of flora and fauna** across the country.
 
• The Tropic of Cancer (23º30' N) passes through the middle of India, impacting its climatic zones.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Latitudinal Extent:**

 
 
• Latitudinal extent refers to the angular distance north or south of the Equator, measured in degrees.
 
• It influences a region's climate, daylight hours, and temperature variations.
 
 
 
• **Tropic of Cancer:**
 
 
• The Tropic of Cancer is located at 23º30' North latitude.
 
• It marks the northernmost point where the sun can be directly overhead.
 
• This line passes through eight Indian states, influencing their climatic patterns.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Climate:**
 
 
• The latitudinal extent affects India's climate, contributing to its diverse climatic zones ranging from tropical in the south to temperate in the north.
 
• Seasonal variations in temperature and precipitation patterns are also influenced by latitude.
 
 
 
• **Day Length Variations:**
 
 
• Day length varies significantly from north to south due to the latitudinal extent.
 
• Regions closer to the Equator experience less variation in day length throughout the year compared to those further north.

questions.question: Which of the following is an ancient Jain text written by Acharya Umaswami that explains the Jain philosophy in the most systematic form acceptable to all sects of Jainism?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tattvarthasutra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Tattvarthasutra** is an ancient Jain text written by Acharya Umaswami (also known as Umasvati).
 
• It is considered the most comprehensive and systematic exposition of Jain philosophy, acceptable to all sects of Jainism.
 
• The text covers various aspects of Jain metaphysics, ethics, and epistemology.
 
• Tattvarthasutra is highly regarded for its clarity and depth in explaining complex philosophical concepts.
 
• The text is divided into ten chapters, each dealing with different aspects of Jain doctrine.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Acharya Umaswami:**

 
 
• Acharya Umaswami was an influential Jain scholar and philosopher.
 
• He is believed to have lived around the 2nd century CE.
 
• His work, Tattvarthasutra, is a cornerstone of Jain literature.
 
 
 
• **Jain Philosophy:**
 
 
• Jain philosophy emphasizes non-violence (Ahimsa), non-possessiveness (Aparigraha), and many-sidedness (Anekantavada).
 
• It provides a detailed account of the soul and its liberation through right belief, knowledge, and conduct.
 
 
 
• **Key Concepts in Tattvarthasutra:**
 
 
• The text explains the "Seven Tattvas" or fundamental principles, including Jiva (soul), Ajiva (non-soul), Asrava (influx of karmas), Bandha (bondage of karmas), Samvara (stoppage of karmas), Nirjara (eradication of karmas), and Moksha (liberation).
 
 
 
• **Relevance:**
 
 
• Tattvarthasutra is used by scholars and practitioners of Jainism for understanding the core tenets of the religion.
 
• It is also referenced in comparative studies of Indian philosophies.

questions.question: What is the name of the new generation ballistic missile with a range of 1,000-2,000 km that was successfully flight tested at APJ Abdul Kalam Island in April 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Agni Prime**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Agni Prime** is a new generation advanced ballistic missile.
 
• It has a range capability of **1,000 to 2,000 kilometers**.
 
• The missile is a part of the **Agni series** developed by the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) of India.
 
• The successful flight test was conducted at **APJ Abdul Kalam Island** in April 2024.
 
• Agni Prime features improved accuracy and advanced technologies compared to its predecessors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Agni Series Missiles**

 
 
• The Agni series includes various strategic ballistic missiles developed by DRDO.
 
• These missiles are designed to enhance India's nuclear deterrence capabilities.
 
• Other missiles in the series include Agni-I, Agni-II, Agni-III, Agni-IV, and Agni-V.
 
• Each missile in the Agni series has different range capabilities, varying from 700 km to over 5,000 km.
 
 
 
• **Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)**
 
 
• DRDO is an agency under the Department of Defence Research and Development in the Ministry of Defence, India.
 
• It is responsible for the development of technology for use by the military.
 
• DRDO's mission is to achieve self-reliance in critical defence technologies and systems.
 
 
 
• **APJ Abdul Kalam Island**
 
 
• Formerly known as Wheeler Island, it is located off the coast of Odisha, India.
 
• It is named after Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam, the 11th President of India and a renowned aerospace scientist.
 
• The island serves as a missile testing facility for DRDO.
 
 
 
• **Ballistic Missile**
 
 
• A ballistic missile follows a sub-orbital flight path to deliver its payload to a predetermined target.
 
• These missiles are categorized based on their range: short-range, medium-range, intermediate-range, and intercontinental.
 
• Ballistic missiles are capable of carrying conventional or nuclear warheads.

questions.question: What is India’s average annual HDI growth for the period 1990-2019?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1.42**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India's average annual Human Development Index (HDI) growth rate from 1990 to 2019 is **1.42%**.
 
• The Human Development Index (HDI) is a summary measure of average achievement in key dimensions of human development: a long and healthy life, being knowledgeable, and having a decent standard of living.
 
• India's HDI value for 2019 was **0.645**, placing it in the medium human development category.
 
• The growth in HDI reflects improvements in life expectancy, education, and per capita income levels over the years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Human Development Index (HDI)**

 
 
• Developed by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and published annually.
 
• It measures and ranks countries' levels of social and economic development based on life expectancy, education, and per capita income indicators.
 
• Countries are classified into four tiers: very high, high, medium, and low human development.
 
 
 
• **Life Expectancy**
 
 
• It is the average number of years a person is expected to live based on the year of their birth, current age, and other demographic factors.
 
• Life expectancy at birth is a key component of the HDI.
 
 
 
• **Education Index**
 
 
• It is calculated using the mean years of schooling for adults aged 25 years and more and the expected years of schooling for children of school-entry age.
 
• This index is a crucial indicator in measuring the education dimension of the HDI.
 
 
 
• **Gross National Income (GNI) per capita**
 
 
• It is the total domestic and foreign output claimed by residents of a country, divided by the population.
 
• GNI per capita is used to measure the standard of living and is a key part of the HDI calculation.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution states that it is the duty of the State to raise the level of nutrition and the standard of living of its people and to improve public health?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 47**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 47** falls under the Directive Principles of State Policy in the Indian Constitution.
 
• It mandates the State to raise the level of nutrition and the standard of living of its people.
 
• The Article also emphasizes the duty of the State to improve public health.
 
• It reflects the commitment of the State to ensure the well-being of its citizens through appropriate policy measures.
 
• Article 47 specifically focuses on the prohibition of the consumption of intoxicating drinks and drugs that are injurious to health, except for medicinal purposes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)**

 
 
• DPSP are guidelines to the central and state governments of India, to be kept in mind while framing laws and policies.
 
• They are enshrined in Part IV (Articles 36-51) of the Indian Constitution.
 
• These principles aim to create social and economic conditions under which citizens can lead a good life.
 
• They are not enforceable by any court, but the principles laid down are considered fundamental in the governance of the country.
 
 
 
• **Public Health Initiatives in India**
 
 
• India has launched several public health programs such as the National Health Mission (NHM) to improve the healthcare system.
 
• Ayushman Bharat is another significant initiative aimed at providing health coverage and establishing wellness centers across the country.
 
• The Government also focuses on immunization programs to prevent diseases like polio, measles, and tuberculosis.
 
• Sanitation and hygiene campaigns like Swachh Bharat Abhiyan aim to improve public health by promoting cleanliness.
 
 
 
• **Nutrition Programs in India**
 
 
• Programs like the Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) aim to improve the nutritional status of children and mothers.
 
• Mid-Day Meal Scheme provides nutritious meals to school children to enhance their nutritional intake and educational outcomes.
 
• POSHAN Abhiyaan is a flagship program to improve nutritional outcomes for children, pregnant women, and lactating mothers.
 
• The Public Distribution System (PDS) ensures the availability of essential food grains to the poor at subsidized rates.

questions.question: When was the second war between the British army and Burma started?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1852**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Second Anglo-Burmese War started in **1852**.
 
• This conflict was initiated due to disputes over the implementation of the Treaty of Yandabo and British interests in Burma.
 
• The war resulted in the annexation of Pegu, leading to the establishment of British control over Lower Burma.
 
• The war ended in **1853** with the British gaining substantial territorial control.
 
• The annexation significantly impacted the region's political landscape, paving the way for further British expansion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **First Anglo-Burmese War**

 
 
• Lasted from 1824 to 1826.
 
• Concluded with the Treaty of Yandabo, which imposed heavy indemnities on Burma.
 
• Resulted in the cession of territories including Assam, Manipur, Arakan, and Tenasserim to the British.
 
 
 
• **Third Anglo-Burmese War**
 
 
• Occurred in 1885.
 
• Led to the complete annexation of Burma into British India.
 
• Resulted from British commercial interests and the desire to preclude French influence in the region.
 
 
 
• **British Colonial Administration**
 
 
• Burma was administered as a province of British India until 1937.
 
• Post-1937, Burma became a separately administered colony.
 
• British rule significantly impacted Burma's socio-economic structures and cultural landscape.
 
 
 
• **Impact of British Rule**
 
 
• Introduced Western education and legal systems.
 
• Development of infrastructure such as railways and ports.
 
• Economic exploitation and changes in land ownership patterns.
 
• Rise of nationalist movements leading to Burma's independence in 1948.

questions.question: According to Environment Performance Index (EPI) 2024, what was India's rank in greenhouse gas production in May 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3rd**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India ranked **3rd** in greenhouse gas production according to the Environment Performance Index (EPI) 2024.
 
• The EPI is a biennial report by Yale and Columbia Universities in collaboration with the World Economic Forum.
 
• The ranking is based on 32 performance indicators across 11 issue categories.
 
• Greenhouse gas emissions are a significant factor in assessing a country's environmental health and climate change mitigation.
 
• China and the United States hold the top two positions respectively in greenhouse gas production.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Environment Performance Index (EPI)**

 
 
• The EPI is a method to quantify and numerically mark the environmental performance of a country's policies.
 
• The index is a joint initiative between Yale University and Columbia University.
 
• It incorporates data from international organizations such as the World Bank and the World Health Organization.
 
• The EPI covers 180 countries and ranks them based on environmental health and ecosystem vitality.
 
 
 
• **Greenhouse Gases (GHGs)**
 
 
• GHGs are gases that trap heat in the atmosphere, leading to the greenhouse effect and global warming.
 
• Key GHGs include carbon dioxide (CO₂), methane (CH₄), nitrous oxide (N₂O), and fluorinated gases.
 
• Human activities such as burning fossil fuels, deforestation, and industrial processes increase GHG concentrations.
 
• Mitigating GHG emissions is crucial for combating climate change.
 
 
 
• **Climate Change Mitigation**
 
 
• Climate change mitigation involves efforts to reduce or prevent the emission of GHGs.
 
• Strategies include transitioning to renewable energy sources, enhancing energy efficiency, and adopting sustainable practices.
 
• International agreements such as the Paris Agreement aim to unite countries in reducing global GHG emissions.
 
• Effective climate policies can help stabilize global temperatures and prevent adverse environmental impacts.

questions.question: Performance Grading Index, which is designed to catalyse transformational change in the field of school education, comprises of ____ indicators.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Performance Grading Index (PGI) is a comprehensive tool designed to assess the performance of states and union territories in the field of school education.
 
• The PGI comprises a total of 70 indicators that evaluate various aspects of school education.
 
• These indicators are grouped into two categories: Outcomes and Governance & Management.
 
• The PGI aims to provide insights into the strengths and areas for improvement in the education system, thereby catalyzing transformational change.
 
• The ultimate goal of the PGI is to ensure that the benefits of quality education reach all students across the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Education Policy (NEP) 2020:**

 
 
• NEP 2020 aims to transform India into a vibrant knowledge society and global knowledge superpower by making both school and college education more holistic, flexible, multidisciplinary, aligned to the needs of the 21st century, and aimed at bringing out the unique capabilities of each student.
 
• It emphasizes the need for early childhood care and education, foundational literacy and numeracy, curricular integration of essential subjects and skills, and the revision and revamping of all aspects of the education structure.
 
 
 
• **Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan:**
 
 
• Samagra Shiksha is an integrated scheme for school education extending from pre-school to class XII.
 
• The scheme aims to ensure inclusive and equitable quality education at all levels of school education.
 
 
 
• **Right to Education (RTE) Act:**
 
 
• The RTE Act, 2009 mandates free and compulsory education for children between the ages of 6 to 14 under Article 21A of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It ensures that education is accessible and available to all children without discrimination.
 
 
 
• **Mid-Day Meal Scheme:**
 
 
• Launched in 1995, the Mid-Day Meal Scheme aims to enhance the enrollment, retention, and attendance of primary and upper primary students in government and government-aided schools.
 
• It provides nutritious meals to children, thereby addressing classroom hunger and enhancing their nutritional status.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution provides for 'Right to work, to education and to public assistance in certain cases'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 41**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 41 of the Indian Constitution is a part of the Directive Principles of State Policy.
 
• It provides for the right to work, to education, and to public assistance in certain cases.
 
• This Article directs the State to make effective provisions for securing the right to work and education, especially for the elderly, sick, and unemployed.
 
• Article 41 emphasizes the role of economic capacity and development in ensuring these rights.
 
• It is a non-justiciable right, meaning it cannot be enforced by the courts but aims to guide the government in policy-making.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)**

 
 
• DPSPs are guidelines for the framing of laws by the government and are non-justiciable.
 
• They are included in Part IV of the Indian Constitution, from Articles 36 to 51.
 
• The aim of DPSPs is to create social and economic conditions under which citizens can lead a good life.
 
• They are inspired by the Directive Principles of the Irish Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Fundamental Rights**
 
 
• Fundamental Rights are enshrined in Part III of the Indian Constitution, from Articles 12 to 35.
 
• They are justiciable, meaning they can be enforced by the courts.
 
• They guarantee civil liberties to all citizens, protecting them against any arbitrary actions of the state.
 
• Key rights include the right to equality, freedom, against exploitation, freedom of religion, cultural and educational rights, and the right to constitutional remedies.
 
 
 
• **Right to Education (RTE)**
 
 
• Article 21A of the Indian Constitution provides for free and compulsory education for children aged 6 to 14 years.
 
• The Right to Education Act (RTE) was enacted in 2009 to enforce this provision.
 
• The Act mandates that private schools reserve 25% of their seats for children from disadvantaged groups.
 
• It aims to improve the quality and accessibility of education across the country.

questions.question: What is the estimated worth of the National Monetization Pipeline unveiled by the Government of India in September 2021?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**₹6 lakh crore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The National Monetization Pipeline (NMP) was unveiled by the Government of India in September 2021.
 
• The NMP aims to unlock value in brownfield projects by engaging the private sector, transferring to them revenue rights but not ownership in the projects.
 
• The estimated worth of the assets to be monetized under the NMP is ₹6 lakh crore.
 
• The pipeline includes sectors such as roads, railways, power, oil and gas pipelines, telecom, civil aviation, ports, and warehousing.
 
• The initiative is expected to help raise resources for future infrastructure investment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Brownfield Projects:**

 
 
• These are existing infrastructure assets that require investment for operation, maintenance, and expansion.
 
• Brownfield projects are less risky compared to greenfield projects as they already have an established structure and revenue stream.
 
 
 
• **Public-Private Partnership (PPP):**
 
 
• A collaborative investment model between government and private sector companies.
 
• It aims to leverage the efficiency, expertise, and capital of the private sector for public projects.
 
 
 
• **Asset Monetization:**
 
 
• The process of generating revenue through existing assets by transferring their usage rights while retaining ownership.
 
• It helps in efficiently utilizing underused or surplus assets.
 
 
 
• **Infrastructure Development:**
 
 
• Essential for economic growth, infrastructure includes transportation, communication, sewage, water, and electric systems.
 
• Improved infrastructure leads to better connectivity, increased productivity, and higher quality of life.

questions.question: The Gita is incorporated in the Mahabharata primarily to give an integrated view of ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dharma**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Bhagavad Gita, often referred to simply as the Gita, is a 700-verse Hindu scripture that is part of the Indian epic Mahabharata.
 
• The Gita is primarily a conversation between Prince Arjuna and the god Krishna, who serves as his charioteer.
 
• This conversation takes place on the battlefield just before the Kurukshetra War, where Krishna imparts spiritual wisdom and guidance to Arjuna.
 
• The core theme of the Gita is "Dharma," which refers to the righteous path or duty. It emphasizes following one's duty according to one's role in life without attachment to the results.
 
• The Gita integrates various paths of yoga (devotion, action, and knowledge) to explain the concept of Dharma and the importance of righteous living.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dharma:** In Hinduism, Dharma signifies behaviors that are considered to be in accord with the order that makes life and the universe possible, including duties, rights, laws, conduct, virtues, and "right way of living".
 
• **Kurukshetra War:** The epic battle depicted in the Mahabharata, fought between two groups of cousins, the Kauravas and the Pandavas, for the throne of Hastinapura.
 
• **Krishna:** A major deity in Hinduism, worshipped as the eighth avatar of the god Vishnu and also as the supreme God in his own right. In the Gita, Krishna serves as Arjuna's charioteer and guide.
 
• **Yoga:** The Gita discusses various paths of yoga (Bhakti Yoga, Karma Yoga, and Jnana Yoga) as ways to realize one's spiritual duties and align with Dharma.
 
• **Mahabharata:** One of the two major Sanskrit epics of ancient India, the other being the Ramayana. It narrates the struggle for sovereignty between the Kauravas and the Pandavas.

questions.question: According to a National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) report, which was the most corrupted state in India in December 2023?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajasthan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) report, Rajasthan was reported as the most corrupted state in India as of December 2023.
 
• The report indicated that Rajasthan had the highest number of registered corruption cases.
 
• Corruption cases in Rajasthan primarily involved public servants and government officials.
 
• The NCRB data is collected from state and union territory police departments, ensuring accurate and up-to-date information.
 
• The increase in corruption cases in Rajasthan has led to heightened scrutiny and calls for stricter anti-corruption measures.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB)**

 
 
• The NCRB is an Indian government agency responsible for collecting and analyzing crime data.
 
• It operates under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
 
• NCRB publishes annual reports on various crimes, including corruption.
 
• The data helps in understanding crime trends and formulating policies for crime prevention and law enforcement.
 
 
 
• **Corruption in India**
 
 
• Corruption is the abuse of entrusted power for private gain.
 
• It affects various sectors, including government, public services, and businesses.
 
• Common forms of corruption include bribery, embezzlement, and nepotism.
 
• Efforts to combat corruption include legal frameworks, watchdog organizations, and public awareness campaigns.
 
 
 
• **Anti-Corruption Measures in India**
 
 
• The Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, is the primary legislation to combat corruption in India.
 
• Other measures include the establishment of the Lokpal and Lokayuktas, and the Central Vigilance Commission (CVC).
 
• Public participation and whistleblower protection are crucial in fighting corruption.
 
• Technology and e-governance are increasingly being used to reduce opportunities for corruption.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Corruption**
 
 
• Corruption undermines economic development and growth.
 
• It leads to a loss of public trust in government institutions.
 
• Corruption increases inequality and reduces the effectiveness of public services.
 
• Efforts to curb corruption can improve governance and promote social justice.

questions.question: When did the British Navy take over Rangoon in British India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sat May 01 1824 00:00:00 GMT+0553 (India Standard Time)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Rangoon (now Yangon) was taken over by the British Navy during the First Anglo-Burmese War.
 
• The capture occurred on **May 1, 1824**, marking a significant point in the conflict.
 
• This event was part of the British Empire's expansion in Southeast Asia.
 
• The British aimed to control important trade routes and resources in the region.
 
• Rangoon was a strategic location due to its proximity to the Irrawaddy River, which was vital for trade and military movements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **First Anglo-Burmese War (1824-1826)**

 
 
• It was the first of three wars fought between the British and Burmese empires.
 
• The war resulted in British control over parts of Burma, including Arakan and Tenasserim.
 
• This conflict was driven by British interests in expanding their influence in Asia.
 
• The Treaty of Yandabo, signed in 1826, ended the war and formalized British territorial gains.
 
 
 
• **British Colonial Expansion**
 
 
• The British Empire expanded its territories through military conquest and strategic treaties.
 
• Southeast Asia, including Burma, became a focal point for British trade and resource extraction.
 
• Control over key locations like Rangoon facilitated British dominance in regional trade.
 
 
 
• **Irrawaddy River**
 
 
• The Irrawaddy River is the largest and most important river in Myanmar (Burma).
 
• It serves as a critical waterway for trade and transportation within the country.
 
• The river's strategic importance made Rangoon a valuable asset for the British.
 
 
 
• **British Naval Operations**
 
 
• The British Navy played a crucial role in securing key ports and coastal areas during colonial expansion.
 
• Naval superiority allowed the British to project power and control over distant territories.
 
• Operations like the capture of Rangoon were part of broader military strategies in the region.

questions.question: Devendra Jhajharia is associated to which of the following games?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Javelin throw**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Devendra Jhajharia is a prominent Indian Paralympic javelin thrower.
 
• He is the first Indian Paralympian to win two gold medals at the Paralympics, achieving this feat in 2004 (Athens) and 2016 (Rio).
 
• Devendra holds the world record in the F46 javelin throw event with a throw of 63.97 meters, which he set during the 2016 Rio Paralympics.
 
• He has been honored with several awards, including the Padma Shri in 2012 and the Padma Bhushan in 2022, recognizing his contributions to sports in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Paralympic Games**

 
 
• The Paralympic Games are a major international multi-sport event involving athletes with a range of disabilities, including impaired muscle power, limb deficiency, and visual impairment.
 
• The Paralympics are held immediately following the Olympic Games, using the same venues and facilities.
 
• The International Paralympic Committee (IPC) is the global governing body of the Paralympic Movement.
 
• The first official Paralympic Games were held in Rome in 1960.
 
 
 
• **F46 Category**
 
 
• This category is for athletes with upper limb deficiencies, including amputations and similar impairments.
 
• Javelin throwers in this category compete with certain modifications to accommodate their impairments.
 
• The classification system ensures fair competition among athletes with different types of disabilities.
 
 
 
• **Indian Paralympic Achievements**
 
 
• India has been participating in the Paralympic Games since 1968.
 
• Indian Paralympians have won medals in various sports, including athletics, swimming, and powerlifting.
 
• The country has seen a steady increase in the number of athletes qualifying for the Games and winning medals.
